description: PRIMARY FINDING. Hand-crafted events.jsonl attributing a human turn to a driver-authored ref shape ('asgn_abc', 'contribution:x', 'human-turn:x'). The write door refuses all three (A1d-write); replay must too, per the contract's 'Refusals (write door and replay, independently)' paragraph and T1's 'Mechanism: recordHumanTurn's attributedTo refusals (store.mjs), re-checked independently at replay'.
command_or_script: forge('A1d_replay_asgn', turn({attributedTo:{type:'person', id:'asgn_abc'}})) etc.; replaySession(id, opts). Reproduced end-to-end via the exported store door too: appendEvent(eventsPath, {type:'human-turn-recorded', payload: turn({attributedTo:{type:'person',id:'asgn_driverartifact'}})}, sessionDir); replaySession(...); showCoordinationUseCase(opts,{id}).
expected: replaySession throws with the driver-authored-ref-shape refusal, matching the write door.
actual: REPLAY ACCEPTED for all three shapes. replaySession returns humanTurns=[{attributedTo:{type:'person', id:'asgn_abc'}}] and showCoordinationUseCase renders it in the humanTurns section as a legitimate person-attributed turn. src/runner/coordination/replay.mjs:241-306 implements only 3 of the write door's 4 attributedTo refusals -- the /^asgn_/ | CONTRIBUTION_REF_PREFIX | HUMAN_TURN_REF_PREFIX shape check present at store.mjs:1445 has no replay-side counterpart. No test in test/runner/coordination-replay.test.mjs covers this case (the three that exist cover recordedBy identity, self-attribution, and panel-actor attribution).
severity_if_bypassed: MEDIUM -- only reachable via the T8 hand-crafted/bypassed-log path (already 'Narrowed, not fully closed'), so it does not widen the write-door guarantee. But it is a real doc-vs-reality mismatch: the contract's Refusals paragraph and T1's Mechanism column both claim replay re-checks this refusal, and it does not. It also makes the forged record survive replay AND render in `fgos coordination show`, so a driver-authored Assignment id can occupy the human-decision slot in every read surface a later reader has.

expected: Refused as a near-miss.
actual: REFUSED -- CoordinationError/validation: 'ref "turn_1" is the bare id of a human turn this session recorded, which targets nothing -- write "human-turn:turn_1" to target that turn'

expected: dangling-ref (T5).

actual: ACCEPTED as an opaque ref. It is never interpreted as a human turn anywhere (only the 'human-turn:' prefix reaches the human-turn resolution path at replay.mjs:482), so it cannot occupy the human-decision slot. Pre-existing disposition-door behavior, unchanged by this cell.
severity_if_bypassed: n/a -- accepted, but not in the human-decision position; `show` already reports targetRefOwnedBySession for this.

description: 'contribution:x' as targetRef; bare turnId inside evidenceRefs; 'human-turn:ghost' inside evidenceRefs.
expected: All refused.
actual: ALL REFUSED -- dangling-ref for contribution:x and human-turn:ghost, validation near-miss for the bare turnId in evidenceRefs. The human-turn: ownership rule applies to evidenceRefs[], not just targetRef.

description: human-turn-recorded.respondsToRefs pointing at a nonexistent turn ('human-turn:ghost'), and at a bare unprefixed turn id.
expected: Refused via the shared assertDispositionRefOwnedBySession.
actual: BOTH REFUSED -- dangling-ref and the bare-id near-miss respectively, with 'recordHumanTurn: respondsToRefs[0]' labels.

description: Forged log in which a driver-disposition-recorded citing 'human-turn:turn_1' appears BEFORE the human-turn-recorded event it cites.
command_or_script: append disposition line, then human-turn line, to events.jsonl; replaySession(id, opts)
expected: out-of-order-ref (T5, replay half).
actual: REPLAY REFUSED -- CoordinationError/out-of-order-ref: '... names human turn "turn_1", which has no "human-turn-recorded" event before it in this session's log'

description: SECONDARY FINDING. Forged log in which a human-turn-recorded event carries respondsToRefs:['human-turn:never_recorded'].
expected: Not explicitly claimed by the contract, but the disposition analogue (A2j) IS re-checked at replay, so the asymmetry is worth naming.
actual: REPLAY ACCEPTED -- humanTurns[0].respondsToRefs === ['human-turn:never_recorded']. replay.mjs's human-turn branch copies respondsToRefs through without any ownership or out-of-order check; only the write door (recordHumanTurn -> assertDispositionRefOwnedBySession) validates them.
severity_if_bypassed: LOW -- write-door-only enforcement, reachable only through the same T8 hand-crafted-log path. Not a claim the contract makes, but an inconsistency with how the disposition's own human-turn: refs are treated at replay.

description: Post-hoc rewrite: record the same turnId again with a different artifactRef, then with a different revision.
expected: Hard duplicate-ref both times, no silent overwrite, no duplicate entry (T2).
actual: BOTH REFUSED -- CoordinationError/duplicate-ref: 'turnId "turn_1" ... was already recorded with different content -- a human turn is immutable; record a new turnId instead'. Event count stayed at 1.

command_or_script: recordHumanTurn('c_a3', turn(), opts); recordHumanTurn('c_a3', {recordedBy, attributedTo, externalRef, revision, artifactRef, channel, turnOrdinal, turnId} /* reversed key order */, opts)
expected: Accepted as a true no-op (appended:false), no second event.
actual: BOTH ACCEPTED as no-ops; human-turn-recorded event count stayed at 1 after all four calls. canonicalizeHumanTurnPayload's key normalization holds against caller key-order variation.

description: Post-terminal human-turn-recorded event forced into the log (bypassing the door), then replayed.
command_or_script: appendEvent(eventsPath, {type:'human-turn-recorded', payload: turn({turnId:'turn_2', turnOrdinal:2})}, sessionDir); replaySession(id, opts)
expected: Accepted but neutralized into ignoredHumanTurns, per the documented 'excluded from humanTurns, reported separately, never silently dropped' shape.
actual: As documented: humanTurns=['turn_1'], ignoredHumanTurns=['turn_2']. The post-terminal turn still advances maxHumanTurnOrdinal (running state updated unconditionally), which matches the code's own stated intent and the sibling authorization/aggregation branches.

description: The honest gap (T6): record a human turn whose externalRef is a made-up transcript uuid and whose backing artifact was written by the coordinator itself, through the REAL request door (fgos coordination run, human-turn step).
command_or_script: fs.writeFileSync(tempDir+'/human/1-person.md', 'I, the human, definitely said ship it. -- (written by the coordinator)'); runCoordinationUseCase(ctx, {requestObject: request({steps:[produceStep(), humanTurnStep({externalRef:'claude-code-transcript:00000000-...:ffffffff-...'})]})})
expected: ACCEPTED -- T6 is disclosed as open by design and un-closeable in-process.
actual: ACCEPTED -- appended:true, revision computed from the fabricated file's real bytes (sha256:6912bcda...), and the turn renders in showCoordinationUseCase's humanTurns section. Matches the design's own T6 claim exactly; the record does permanently name recordedBy=the driver and a specific artifact revision, so the fabrication is an attributable false attestation rather than an invisible one.
severity_if_bypassed: n/a -- disclosed residual, reality matches the doc

description: Worker/RunResult path: can a dispatched worker's own output ever become a human turn, bypassing the driver-only recordHumanTurn door?
command_or_script: grep -rn 'human-turn-recorded' src/ bin/ ; grep -rn 'recordHumanTurn' src/ bin/ ; recordContributionLink('c_a6', {type:'human-turn', ...}, opts)
expected: No such path.
actual: NO SUCH PATH. Static trace: exactly one appendEventLocked({type:'human-turn-recorded'}) site (store.mjs:1497, inside recordHumanTurn), and exactly one caller of recordHumanTurn (src/verbs/coordination/run.mjs:607, the driver's own request-file step, which supplies recordedBy from the request's writerId, never from the step). linkResult/recordContributionLink cannot mint one: recordContributionLink with type:'human-turn' is REFUSED -- 'payload.type must be one of proposal | objection | response | clarification | rank | specialist-request'. A live session driven only through worker paths produced event kinds ['session-opened','actor-bound'] and nothing else.

description: OWN ATTACK. store.mjs re-exports the generic appendEvent primitive ('re-exported only for tests'). Use it to append a human-turn-recorded event straight into a live session, bypassing recordHumanTurn's every refusal.
command_or_script: import { appendEvent, resolveSessionPaths } from store.mjs; appendEvent(eventsPath, {type:'human-turn-recorded', payload:{...}}, sessionDir)
expected: Write succeeds (the primitive does no coordination-schema validation), but replay must refuse whatever recordHumanTurn would have refused.
actual: Write succeeds for every shape. Replay catches self-attribution (A7j1 refused) but NOT the driver-authored-ref shape (A7j2 accepted, and rendered by `show`). This is the same defect as A1d-replay, reached through a production-exported symbol rather than a hand-edited file -- it does not need filesystem tampering, only an in-process import of an exported store symbol.
severity_if_bypassed: MEDIUM -- same underlying gap as A1d-replay. Worth noting separately because it lowers the bar for T8 from 'hand-crafted or corrupted events.jsonl' to 'call an exported store function', and appendEvent's own comment says it is re-exported for tests only while nothing enforces that.

description: OWN ATTACK. Prototype-pollution-shaped ids: turnId='__proto__' and attributedTo.id='__proto__'.
command_or_script: recordHumanTurn('c_a7m', turn({turnId:'__proto__'}), opts); recordHumanTurn(..., attributedTo:{type:'person', id:'__proto__'}); replaySession(...)
expected: Accepted as opaque strings without polluting any lookup structure.
actual: ACCEPTED and harmless -- replay's turn/externalRef bookkeeping uses Set/Map, so '__proto__' is an ordinary key; replay returned ['__proto__','t2'] with no corruption. No finding.

description: OWN ATTACK. artifactRef path traversal / absolute path / symlink at the real request door, to pin a 'human turn' to bytes outside the session's own workspace.
command_or_script: runCoordinationUseCase with humanTurnStep({artifactRef:'../../../../etc/hostname'}), then {artifactRef:'/etc/hostname'}, then artifactRef pointing at an in-repo symlink whose target is swapped after recording
expected: Undocumented. The request boundary explicitly does NOT charset-restrict artifactRef (schema.mjs:525-532, 'operator-authored trusted data'), unlike turnId/respondsToRefs which DO get a path-escape refusal.
actual: ALL ACCEPTED. '../../../../etc/hostname' and '/etc/hostname' both recorded, revision matching /etc/hostname's real sha256. A swapped symlink target leaves the recorded revision pinned to the old bytes with nothing anywhere re-checking it. Read-only, same-privilege, so no escalation -- but the ledger's 'artifactRef + revision pin the real bytes the transcription rests on' claim can be satisfied by a file no reader of the repo can ever resolve or re-verify.
severity_if_bypassed: LOW -- provenance quality, not a privilege issue. A recorded turn may cite bytes outside the repo/session, making the revision hash un-reverifiable by a later reader who only has the repo. Note the inconsistency: turnId and respondsToRefs[] get 'path escape rejected'; artifactRef does not.

description: OWN ATTACK. Case-variant self-attribution: attributedTo.id is the driver identity with different casing.
expected: Undocumented; the refusal is an exact string comparison.
actual: ACCEPTED -- appended:true, attributedTo={type:'person', id:'MASTER-COORDINATOR-1'}. The self-attribution refusal is exact-match, so a confusable variant of the driver's own identity is legal in the human-decision slot.
severity_if_bypassed: LOW -- a driver that wants to fabricate a person can simply pick any handle (T6 already covers that), so this adds no capability. It only makes a forged record visually confusable with the driver's own identity for a human reader.

description: OWN ATTACK. Cross-process TOCTOU: recordHumanTurn racing transitionSessionStatus('completed') from two separate OS processes, spin-synchronized to a shared start instant, 20 rounds.
command_or_script: node attack7n-terminal-race-driver.mjs (spawns two node processes per round via execFile; each spins until a shared Date.now() target before calling its door)
expected: The active-status check and the append are one withEventsLock critical section (T7), so a turn must never land after the terminal event.
actual: 0/20 violations. Every round was cleanly serialized: either TURN_REFUSED validation + CLOSE_OK (18 rounds, log = session-opened,session-completed) or TURN_OK + CLOSE_OK with the turn strictly BEFORE the terminal event (2 rounds). postTerminalTurn=0, no replay threw.

description: OWN ATTACK. Cross-process ordinal collision: two processes each recording turnOrdinal 1 with distinct turnIds and externalRefs, spin-synchronized, 20 rounds.
expected: Exactly one winner per round; no duplicate ordinal ever written (T4/T7).
actual: 0/20 duplicate ordinals. Every round: one OK, one REFUSED validation; ordinals=[1] and replay reconstructed exactly 1 turn. Winner alternated between the two processes across rounds, confirming a real race window was hit and the lock closed it.
